rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement (Rent Ordinance)
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Ordinance Section 37.9(a)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. This includes some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, the landlord may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.interaction_text: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance.
